claims.text: Both sides are arguing about one trip. The trip_record (EV-TRIP-00110), the gps_trace (EV-GPS-00110) and the fare_breakdown (EV-FARE-00110) each carry trip_id TRP-00110, and the trace's first fix at 18:23:40 matches the trip_record's started_at for the same trip. That satisfies the first limb of the rider's burden under POL-RD-08(a) — the artifacts describe the same trip — so this dispute is decidable on this record and is not a case of mismatched bundles.

The driver's own trace is impaired for policy purposes. Between consecutive fixes it carries a 428-second gap (18:35:00 to 18:42:08) against the 90-second limit in POL-RD-07(a), and across that same stretch a 6.9 km straight-line jump against the 500 m limit in POL-RD-07(b); the normal sampling interval is 10 s, so this is one large break, not ordinary noise. If the admissibility pre-pass has down-weighted this artifact on the same defects, that impairment is disclosed here and POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence on any fact the trace alone carries.

Because the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) and (b), a deviation may not be established on it alone under POL-RD-07(ii), and none of the independent corroborating sources that limb names is present: the chat log records no driver admission of leaving the corridor, the driver's only route words are 'going KPE', which is the optimal corridor itself, and the fare_breakdown carries no erp_gantries placing the vehicle on a road the optimal route does not use. With the trace impaired and no corroboration, POL-RD-07(iii) requires ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory, and under POL-GEN-03 escalation is terminal and holds the disputed amount rather than collecting it.

The 2.8 km / 15.2% excess the platform reports sits just under the 20% establishment test in POL-RD-01, but that number cannot be used against the rider as if it were a clean measurement. POL-RD-07(i) requires the excess across the impaired stretch to be measured as the straight line between the bounding fixes — a reading the clause itself calls the one most favourable to the driver — and a straight line is the shortest distance between two fixes. The recorded excess is therefore a floor, not a ceiling, and the record cannot say whether the true excess crosses the POL-RD-01 threshold. That unresolved margin is exactly the data failure POL-RD-07(iii) sends to a human reviewer.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. EV-ADVIS-00110-01 is MISSING — it carries no payload and weight 0.0 — so nothing in the record names a road, expressway segment or junction on the optimal corridor, still less one with a validity window overlapping the trip. Under POL-RD-03 a traffic advisory is the only thing that exonerates a route choice, and a bare 'I took the KPE like always' is not one; with the artifact absent, no external event accounts for the distance the platform billed, and the rider should not carry the cost of a route the driver cannot show was forced on him.

The chat log will not bear the weight of a rider-requested detour either. POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider, timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor, identifying a place or road specifically enough to act on, and corroborated by the trace passing within 200 m of a waypoint_hint. The only rider message here is 'ok'; the message naming the KPE came from the driver; its waypoint_hint is null; and the KPE is on the optimal corridor in any event. The rider-instruction limb fails at its first requirement, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and the excess cannot be excluded as rider-caused.

Nothing on the rider's profile raises the corroboration bar. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 — well below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08 — so the extra-corroboration factor for sub-30% excesses does not apply, and that factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven. That is the only profile field the clause calls on; under POL-GEN-01 every other number on either profile, including the driver's lifetime prior_deviation_flags, is context only and cannot ground a finding.

If the judge resolves the impairment against the driver and finds the excess established, the remedy is not zero. On the platform's own arithmetic the recomputed optimal-route fare is 25.68 against a charged total of 34.42, giving a refund of 8.74 — a PARTIAL_REFUND under POL-RD-02, rounded up to 8.75 and comfortably above the 0.50 de minimis. The rider asks primarily for escalation on this impaired record; this figure is the fallback if the POL-RD-01 threshold is crossed.

claims.text: The rider's claim fails the percentage limb of the POL-RD-01 threshold. The trace distance is 21.2 km against an optimal route of 18.4 km, an excess of 2.8 km, which the platform's own derivation fixes at 15.22% - below the 20% figure POL-RD-01 requires. Both establishment tests must pass, and one of them does not, so no route deviation exists on this trip.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and forbids citing the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The trace records 21.2 km - the same figure, so nothing turns on the choice - and the platform's derived deviation block returns the status 'no deviation'. The rider's '18-19 km' recollection is an estimate, not a measured excess, and cannot supply the threshold.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. The trip identifiers do match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, so limb (a) is satisfied, but limb (b) is not: the excess is 15.2%, not the 20% the threshold demands. The rider also states she 'was on my phone so I did not watch the route', so her account of the route is inference rather than observation, and the trace does not bear it out.

The trace contains a 428-second gap between 18:35:00 and 18:42:08 with a 6.9 km straight-line jump, consistent with the driver's explanation of phone signal loss in the KPE tunnel. POL-RD-07(i) measures the excess across an impaired stretch as the straight line between the bounding fixes - the reading most favourable to the driver - and on that reading the excess is still 2.8 km / 15.2%, below the establishment threshold. There is no qualifying excess for POL-RD-07(ii)-(iii) to operate on.

The chat log records the driver announcing 'going KPE ah boss' at 18:25:50 and the rider answering 'ok' at 18:26:14, roughly two minutes after the trip started and while still on the optimal corridor. KPE is the corridor the platform's own routing engine identifies as optimal ('optimal is KPE then ECP'), so the rider accepted the route that was in fact driven. To the extent POL-RD-04 is engaged, any excess is attributable to a route the rider endorsed in the chat_log.

The $3.00 of ERP the rider flags is a properly chargeable pass-through, not an off-route gantry. The trip_record records the optimal route as 'KPE then ECP, crossing both gantries' with optimal_route_erp_sgd of 3.00, and the fare_breakdown's derived ERP block itemises no off-optimal-route line at all, so nothing here attracts a standalone correction under POL-RD-09.

Even if the tribunal runs the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check, there is no pattern to find: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 744, far below the three-flag or 0.05-ratio test. No repeat-deviation uplift and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is available on this record.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION, and under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative: it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status (CHARGED) and refund_issued_sgd (0.00) exactly as they stand. On this rider-filed dispute that preserves the fare the driver earned and issues no refund.

Nothing in this record triggers POL-RD-10. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, so trigger (2) does not fire; the timestamps are internally consistent (first and last fixes equal the recorded start and end, charge posted 18 seconds after dropoff), so trigger (4) does not fire; and trigger (3) is not engaged because the case is not resolved by asking whether a deviation can be established from an impaired trace - POL-RD-01 resolves it on the threshold, which the excess fails on any reading of the derived figures.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the driver's own GPS trace records 21.2 km against a booked optimal route of 18.4 km — an excess of 2.8 km, or 15.2%, below the 20% (3.68 km) the route-deviation threshold needs — and the platform's derivation prints 'no deviation'. In an ordinary case that would end the matter; it does not here. Between 18:35:00 and 18:42:08 the trace has a 428-second gap, across which it jumps 6.9 km in a straight line — more than a third of the whole trip, and consistent with the driver's KPE-tunnel signal loss. POL-RD-07 makes that trace impaired for policy purposes, and over the impaired stretch the distance cannot be measured: 21.2 km is the shortest, driver-favourable reading, so the true excess could be larger and the 20% test cannot be decided either way. Where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(b) and no independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii) corroborates the route — and none does: the chat log records no detour admission (the only route words are the driver's 'going KPE', which is the optimal corridor itself), the fare breakdown charges no off-route gantry, and trip_record.actual_distance_km is a copy of the same trace — POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) require ESCALATE rather than a dismissal. Your case is not rejected; it goes to a human reviewer, and the disputed $34.42 is held, not collected or refunded.

To the driver: nothing here finds you detoured. Your 'going KPE' is the optimal corridor, the $3.00 of ERP lies on the optimal route with no off-route gantry billed, and no traffic advisory exists either to exonerate or to implicate you (EV-ADVIS-00110-01 is empty, weight 0.0). This escalation is a data failure, not a finding against you.

Figures used: trace_distance_km 21.2, optimal_distance_km 18.4, excess 2.8 km / 15.2%, charged_total $34.42, recomputed optimal-route fare $25.68, and — only if a deviation were later established — a POL-RD-02 refund of $8.75; that fallback is not this ruling. No referral fires: POL-RD-06 is not engaged (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 744 completed trips), and there is no unmatched billing line to refer under POL-RD-09(4). What would resolve this: the route map support could not produce, a trace that covers the tunnel, or an independent record — a charged off-route gantry, or a chat admission of a detour — placing the vehicle off the optimal corridor.

To both parties: the SGD 34.42 fare is HELD and this case goes to a human reviewer. No refund and no further charge issues - POL-GEN-03 makes escalation terminal.

The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00110) is impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries a 428-second gap between consecutive fixes (18:35:00 to 18:42:08) against the 90-second limit in limb (a), and a 6.9 km straight-line jump across that same gap against the 500 m limit in limb (b), where the normal sampling interval is 10 seconds. About a third of the 21.2 km driven is therefore unobserved, and the platform's excess figure - 2.8 km, or 15.22% over the 18.4 km optimal - is produced by interpolating straight across that unobserved stretch, the reading POL-RD-07(i) calls the one most favourable to the driver.

Because the trace is impaired, POL-RD-07(ii) forbids establishing a deviation on the trace alone; it needs one of four independent sources, and none exists. (1) The chat log (EV-CHAT-00110) contains no driver admission of leaving the corridor - the driver's only route words, 'going KPE ah boss', name the optimal corridor itself, which the trip record's routing engine records as 'optimal is KPE then ECP'. (2) The fare breakdown's ERP block itemises no gantry at all (off-optimal-route ERP total 0.00), so it places the vehicle nowhere. (3) The counterparty statement admits nothing - 'I took the KPE like always' is again the optimal corridor. (4) The trip record's actual_distance_km (21.2 km) is the same measurement as the trace figure (21.2 km), so it is not independent corroboration.

With the trace impaired and no corroboration, POL-RD-07(iii) directs ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION - the missing proof is a data failure, not a finding for the driver - and POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory. The trigger that fired is POL-RD-10(3). What would resolve it: an independent record of the route taken through the 18:35-18:42 gap, such as a charged gantry off the KPE/ECP corridor, a driver admission in the chat log, or a distance the platform derived independently of this trace.

The driver's points, answered together where they make the same point: the POL-RD-01 threshold argument (excess 2.8 km = 15.22%, below the 20% limb, so no deviation) is arithmetically right but does not decide the case, because the reading it rests on is the impaired trace, and POL-RD-07(iii) turns exactly that situation into an escalation instead of a NO_ACTION. The same reasoning answers the POL-RD-08 burden argument - limb (a) is satisfied (all three artifacts carry TRP-00110 and the trace's first fix 18:23:40 matches the trip record's started_at), and limb (b) cannot be assessed from an impaired trace without corroboration. The POL-RD-04 argument fails on its own terms: the only rider message is 'ok', it follows the driver's message, the rider names no place or road, waypoint_hint is null, and the KPE is the optimal corridor, so there is no rider-requested detour to exonerate. The POL-RD-09 argument is accepted: the SGD 3.00 of ERP recorded on the optimal route is a properly chargeable pass-through and no off-route gantry line is itemised, so no standalone correction and no POL-RD-09(4) referral arises. The POL-RD-06 argument is accepted: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 744, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises.

The rider's points: the identification argument is accepted - the trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown all carry TRP-00110 and the trip-record start time matches the trace's first fix, so this is one trip, not a mismatched bundle. The impairment and no-corroboration arguments are accepted and are what decide the case. The argument that the recorded excess is a floor rather than a ceiling is noted, but POL-RD-07(i) fixes the straight-line reading and the escalation rests on the absence of corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii)-(iii), not on the size of the figure. The advisory point is accepted: EV-ADVIS-00110-01 is absent (payload null, weight 0.0), so nothing exonerates the route under POL-RD-03, and 'I took the KPE like always' is not a traffic advisory. The profile point is accepted: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so no extra corroboration bar applies; the driver's lifetime prior_deviation_flags mentioned nearby is context only under POL-GEN-01. The fallback refund of 8.74, rounded up to 8.75, is not reached - escalation is terminal and no money issues.

Confidence is 0.70. The facts that carry this ruling - the trace's impairment and the absence of corroboration - rest on artifacts at full weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-00110, EV-CHAT-00110, EV-FARE-00110, EV-TRIP-00110), so nothing caps confidence below that; it is placed at the platform floor because the record itself cannot say whether a deviation occurred - a third of the trip is unobserved, and neither a finding for the rider nor a clean finding for the driver would be safe.

To the rider and the driver: this case goes to a human reviewer. No money moves either way while that review is pending — the $34.42 you were charged is held, neither collected nor refunded.

What follows is POL-RD-07(ii): with the trace impaired, a deviation may not be established on the trace alone and must be corroborated by an independent source. (b) The fare breakdown's ERP lines place the vehicle on no off-optimal corridor: there are no gantry lines to match, and the $3.00 ERP is a properly chargeable pass-through that the trip record itself records as lying on the optimal route. With the trace impaired and no corroboration, POL-RD-07(iii) requires ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, and POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory. That is the trigger that fired.

But that 15.22% is read off the impaired trace, and POL-RD-07(i) requires the excess across the impaired stretch to be measured as the straight line between the bounding fixes — the shortest possible reading, which the clause itself calls the one most favourable to the driver. The derived excess is therefore a floor, not a clean result, and the record cannot say whether the true excess crosses the 20% threshold. That unresolved margin is a data failure, not a finding for the driver, which is why the clause sends it to a reviewer instead of leaving the charge standing. For the same reason the rider's POL-RD-08(b) burden cannot be concluded either way: the excess must be shown from an unimpaired trace or, on an impaired one, from a POL-RD-07(ii) source, and neither exists.

POL-RD-04 is unavailable: the only rider message is 'ok', no waypoint_hint is attached, and a rider instruction must name a place or road specifically enough to act on — and the KPE is on the optimal corridor in any event, so nothing needs excluding as rider-caused. POL-RD-09 yields no standalone correction: no gantry line is unmatched, and the ERP match is undecidable on this record, which the clause says means the line is treated as matched. The rider's fallback figure — recomputed fare 25.68 against a charged total of 34.42, a refund of 8.74 rounded up to 8.75 — is not applied, because the threshold question it depends on cannot be answered on this record; it is the figure that would be used if the threshold were established.

Confidence. The fact this escalation rests on — the trace impairment — is carried by EV-GPS-00110, which bears no admissibility discount, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and I record 0.90. bundle_integrity_score is context only and is not the cap.

What would resolve it: a corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names — ERP gantry data placing the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use, a driver admission in the chat log, or a distance measurement the platform derived independently of this trace — or a repaired trace covering the 18:35–18:42 stretch. Escalation is terminal under POL-GEN-03: both money fields are null and the disputed amount is held.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both of you. I cannot decide this case on the record, so it goes to a human reviewer. The disputed S$34.42 is held — not collected from the rider and not refunded to her — and no compensation is ordered.

The arithmetic. The platform's own figures put the trip at 21.2 km (the GPS trace, EV-GPS-00110) against an optimal route of 18.4 km (EV-TRIP-00110): an excess of 2.8 km, or 15.2%. POL-RD-01 requires an excess over 20% AND over 0.8 km together. If those figures could be relied on, the rider's claim would fail and the charge would stand — I have the driver's argument to that effect (POL-RD-01, POL-RD-08) well in mind.

Why they cannot be relied on. The trace carries a 428-second gap between consecutive fixes (18:35:00 to 18:42:08) and a 6.9 km straight-line jump across it, on a trace sampled every 10 seconds. POL-RD-07(a) and (b) set 90 seconds and 500 metres. The trace is therefore impaired for policy purposes. I record both required things (POL-GEN-02(3)): the pre-pass did not down-weight it — it still carries weight 1.0 and no claim had to disclose an impairment — and it is impaired under POL-RD-07 all the same.

What follows. POL-RD-07(i) reads the impaired stretch as the straight line between the bounding fixes, the reading most favourable to the driver. That makes 2.8 km / 15.2% a floor, not a measured excess: the vehicle's true path across those 6.9 km is unknown, so the threshold test cannot be concluded either way on this record. The rider is right on that point.

POL-RD-07(ii) then requires an independent source, and I checked each one it names. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00110) contains the driver's 'going KPE ah boss' and the rider's 'ok'; the KPE is the optimal corridor, so this is not an admission of a detour. The fare breakdown itemises no ERP gantry at all, so no charged crossing places the vehicle off the optimal corridor. The driver's statement admits taking the KPE — again the optimal corridor — and blames tunnel signal loss, but admits no deviating route. And trip_record.actual_distance_km (21.2 km) is the same figure as the trace, a copy, not an independent measurement. There is no corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names.

Under POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) that means ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, and escalation is terminal (POL-GEN-03).

The remaining claims. The trip identifiers and start times match across the three artifacts (the rider's POL-RD-08(a) point) — accepted. The driver's threshold and 'no deviation' points are correct arithmetic but rest on the broken trace, so they do not decide the case. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00110-01, weight 0.0, no payload) means POL-RD-03 cannot exonerate the driver — accepted — but it supplies nothing the rider needs either. The chat shows no rider-requested detour: the KPE message came from the driver, waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 neither exonerates nor compensates. The $3.00 of ERP sits on the optimal route (optimal_route_erp_sgd 3.00 in EV-TRIP-00110), so no pass-through correction is due on it. Nothing raises the corroboration bar on the rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d 1, below POL-RD-08's 4-claim trigger). There is no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 744), so no POL-RD-06 uplift and no conduct referral. The rider's fallback refund figure (8.74, rounded to 8.75) is not reached. The driver's prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is context only under POL-GEN-01; I have not used it. The driver's statement carries no weight_multiplier, so it moves neither the floor nor the cap, but it has been considered as evidence.

Open questions for the reviewer, which belong here rather than in the referrals list: where the vehicle actually was between 18:35:00 and 18:42:08 and whether it stayed on the KPE/ECP corridor; and a reconciliation of the ERP accounting, since the fare breakdown's ERP block totals 0.00 while $3.00 of tolls was charged, and the platform's recomputed_fare of 25.68 appears to omit the $3.00 optimal-route ERP that EV-TRIP-00110 records (including it gives 28.68 and a refund of about 5.75).
